source.title: What do larger image classifiers memorise?
source.authors: Michal Lukasik; Vaishnavh Nagarajan; A. S. Rawat; A. Menon; Sanjiv Kumar

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: It empirically sweeps image-classifier model sizes and reports training/test accuracy and a stability-based per-example memorisation measure, a related but different operationalization from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures stability-based memorisation (the effect of including a training example) and model-size trends, not fitting random labels. Its CIFAR-100 train/test accuracy table directly bears on V2's width/size proposition; the memorisation-score distributions and proxies are not the train–test gap measure named by V7. Rows below include the separate reported one-hot CIFAR-100 train/test accuracies by model size and the reported distilled train/test results by teacher–student pair. Other size-sweep memorisation-score plots and per-example trajectory results are described in the text/figures but not numerically recoverable in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures stability-based memorisation across model sizes and under distillation. Its accuracy sweep varies ResNet depth, whereas V2 concerns widening beyond the width needed for interpolation. Its width experiments report memorisation distributions, without the post-interpolation test-error comparison V2 requires. None of V1–V8 is directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but the depth-accuracy result is supporting context. The central conclusions are that memorisation distributions become more bimodal with capacity, individual examples follow diverse trajectories, and correlated proxies miss these patterns. Distillation tends to inhibit memorisation, particularly on increasing-trajectory examples, while often improving generalisation. The proposed explanation of why distillation improves generalisation is supported by this association rather than established causally.
record.recipe_differences: Standard minibatch SGD image-classification size sweep on CIFAR-100; it studies ResNet depth and stability-based per-example memorisation, rather than one-hidden-layer ReLU width and the interpolation-threshold test-error curve.
record.method_sensitivity: Model depth/size changes average and per-example memorisation; dataset and architecture family are varied in supplementary analyses; distillation changes memorisation and train/test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-100 one-hot ResNets improve test accuracy from 0.57 to 0.73 as depth increases from 8 to 110; depths 44, 56 and 110 have reported training accuracy 1.00.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing ResNet depth can improve held-out accuracy after training accuracy saturates, under the tested regularized and augmented recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorisation-score distributions become increasingly bimodal with model depth or width. Average memorisation declines for sufficiently deep CIFAR-100 models, while some examples have increasing scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capacity changes the distribution and individual trajectories of stability-based memorisation, beyond its average.

fits_no_version.finding: Distillation generally inhibits stability-based memorisation and improves test accuracy, with accuracy exceptions for ResNet-110 teachers distilled into depths 14 and 20. For the ResNet-110-to-32 analysis, 97.2% of examples with reduced memorisation have increasing trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation preferentially reduces stability-based memorisation on examples with increasing memorisation trajectories and often improves held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: C-score proxies and prediction depth correlate with memorisation scores but fail to reproduce their bimodal distributions and capacity-dependent trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlation with stability-based memorisation does not ensure faithful distributional or trajectory measurements.

record.problems: The study is limited to image classification, and its stability-based score requires many model trainings; the authors explicitly note the computational cost. Many distributional and trajectory findings are shown only in figures, without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. The CIFAR-100 train/test accuracy table does not report uncertainty for the one-hot results.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: average memorisation scores and in-sample/out-of-sample component curves in Figure 2; score-distribution histograms and width sweep in Figures 3, 6, 7 and 20; detailed trajectory and proxy comparisons in Figures 1, 4, 8 and 26–28; and per-example distillation score comparisons in Figures 5 and 14–19. These are figure-only or stability-score outcomes and do not directly report the train/test-gap measure named by the mapped versions. Distilled train/test results are retained in rows R8–R19.

untested.parts: No paired fixed-random-label and natural-label experiments measuring training fit and held-out accuracy.

No test-error comparison across widths beyond an established interpolation threshold. The accuracy table varies depth; the width figures measure memorisation distributions. The training recipe also includes weight decay and augmentation.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or manipulation of local connectivity.
No batch-size comparison under matched epoch budgets.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measure or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of the most memorized examples versus matched random removals followed by retraining and test-accuracy evaluation. Estimating inclusion effects does not perform this intervention.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted accuracy values match the supplied tables. Remove both V2 verdicts: depth scaling is not width scaling, and pre-interpolation results are not scope limitations of a post-interpolation claim. No additional result directly bearing on V1–V8 requires a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorisation or paired natural-label generalization experiment.

The paper varies ResNet depth, not one-hidden-layer ReLU width on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; it reports that train accuracy reaches 1.00 and test accuracy improves with depth, but does not identify the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures or of local connectivity.
The study measures a per-example stability-based memorisation score, but does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps.
It does not remove selected memorized examples and retrain to measure test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: It discusses memorisation capacity and generalisation and prior findings about memorised examples, but its own experiments do not test the specified claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study measures stability-based memorisation across capacity and distillation settings without testing V1–V8. Depth-accuracy results do not test V2's width effect; width experiments report memorisation distributions.

source_check.notes: All 19 numerical rows match Tables 5–6. Distillation's accuracy improvements are not universal: the ResNet-110 teacher lowers test accuracy for ResNet-14 and ResNet-20 relative to one-hot training.
